newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Peters says Morgan's move to sell story wrong.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Peters says Morgan's move to sell story wrong.

text.p: Deputy Prime Minister and New Zealand First leader Winston Peters on Thursday publicly rebuked MP Tukoroirangi Morgan over his attempt to sell an interview to two television stations.
Peters said the approaches to the media were plainly wrong and had occurred without his knowledge.

"Mr Morgan's involvement in approaches to the media outlets for an appearance fee motivated by the need to pay legal costs associated with the Aotearoa Television Network affair, occurred without any knowledge of me or my office," Peters said in a statement.
"Had I been approached, I would have told Mr Morgan categorically that such approaches are plainly wrong."
Peters said any repetition of a mistake of this nature "will result in severe consequences".
A lawyer representing Morgan approached TV1 and TV3 on Wednesday seeking payment of more than NZ$20,000 for an interview with Morgan.
In a u-turn on Thursday Morgan admitted he had instructed the lawyer to make the approach. Late on Wednesday Peters told journalists Morgan had told him he had not instructed the lawyer.
In his statement on Thursday Peters said that had been incorrect.
"Whether or not Mr Morgan understood the intent of my questions with respect to his legal advisor, I do not know.
"However the effect of his answer to me led me to believe that there could not be a solicitor-client realtionship and I stated that publicly," Peters said.

Prime Minister Jim Bolger also expressed his dissatisfaction with Morgan's conduct, but did not issue a formal comment. A spokesman for his office told Reuters that Bolger found the MP's behaviour "unacceptable and inappropriate".
Asked how the premier took issue with the move spokesman Richard Griffin said Bolger believed, "That it is not the business of politicans and parliamentarians to be asking for money for interviews.
"They are public persona and as such (media access) is part of the burden of office," he added.
Morgan said on Thursday that he needed to cover the expenses of two defamation cases he was involved which his barrister, Peter Williams QC, said could cost around $100,000 altogether.
